name: m4-tenure
description: The tables under a small young generation: a 2 GB heap with `-Xmn256m`, G1 regions pinned at 4 MB (so the humongous threshold is the 2 MB of an 8 GB heap). Each compile now sees many young GCs, G1's tenuring threshold drops to 1 or 2, and chunks are promoted within a compile, after which inserts into them dirty cards as inserts into the chained table's humongous array do. A local probe at these settings (README, "Keeping chunks young") gave `chunked-weak-rejuv` 673 ms per compile against 736 for `chunked-weak` and 744 for `chained-weak`.
Graal 25.4.4, one fork per table and round, fresh tables per compile.

variantDescriptions.chunked-weak-rejuv: `chunked-weak`, copying each element chunk written at least 256 times since the last GC, so chunks stay young
variantDescriptions.chunked-strong: the chunked layout with strong slots
